title: Opportunity mapping - LLM API deltas
summary: Concise field-facing brief that maps where Redwood should push vs other LLM API providers. Focuses on operational deltas buyers care about (tail latency, predictable cost, rollout controls, private deployments) and converts them into persona-level opportunities and demo motions.
target_personas: Platform engineer - cares about SLAs, routing policies, and rollout isolation
ML infra lead - cares about cost per request, batching, quantization suggestions
Product manager (growth) - cares about latency, streaming UX, and dev velocity
Security/compliance lead - needs VPC/private deploy, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs
buyer_triggers: Bursty production traffic causing high token bills or unpredictable latency
Failed prove-out using single-model hosted provider due to tail-latency or cold-starts
Procurement/regulatory requirement for VPC or on-prem inference
Need to move from research to production with predictable rollout and rollback
primary_differentiators: Predictable performance: SLA-friendly routing, dedicated pools, and tail-latency controls
Unified surface: same API and rollout primitives across hosted, dedicated, and private
Cost levers exposed to engineers: batching/caching recommendations and quantization guidance
Operational visibility: token-level cost and latency breakdown, per-route dashboards
competitor_weaknesses_to_exploit: Opaque unit economics — competitors hide batching/caching assumptions; show real per-conversation math
Single-mode deployments — many can't combine hosted + on-prem fallback without heavy engineering
Weak rollout primitives — canned model swaps without canary/A-B or automatic fallback under pressure
Insufficient observability — lack of token-level cost tracing and prompt-set regression alerts
metric_messaging: Reduce 95th/99th percentile token latency with routing + KV caching (show measured delta for typical convo workloads)
Cut per-conversation cost via recommended batching and quantization profile (sample: 25-40% savings on retrieval-heavy prompts)
Time-to-production: demo a working canary rollout + automated fallback in under 30 minutes
Compliance: show customer-managed control plane and KMS integration checklist for proof
objection_handling: Objection: 'We already use X provider and it's cheaper' -> Answer: Walk through cost model differences: show token-level debug, caching opportunities, and long-tail savings from dedicated capacity
Objection: 'We can't migrate easily' -> Answer: Highlight API parity and migration checklist: model pinning, staged rollouts, and sandboxing with minimal code changes
Objection: 'We're concerned about latency tails' -> Answer: Offer concrete SLOs, show tail-latency charts from similar workloads, and propose a short pilot with representative traffic to validate
Objection: 'We need on-prem for compliance' -> Answer: Explain Private deployment plan, KMS options, audit log accessibility, and professional services handoff
battle_traps: Competitor points to model catalog breadth — flip to runtime economics and quality-control (we optimize kernel selection + quantization profiles for production workloads)
Competitor touts cheaper per-token rate — trap: they assume maximal batching and ignore latency or cache-miss patterns; show real customer profile where we win
Competitor promises 'instant scale' — probe for expected tail SLA and multi-region redundancy; push for documented SLAs and rollback behavior
demo_checklist: Baseline: sample app using competitor API with identifiable real traces (5–10 convo examples)
Instrumented comparison: token-level logging, latency histogram, cost-per-session calc
Showcase: canary rollout switching one route to Redwood with zero code changes and automatic fallback
Ops story: open console, drill into per-route cost, show regression alerts tied to eval set

field_notes: Early conversations with fintech prospect: procurement demands KMS + quarterly audit; emphasize Private and professional services model
Large marketplace customer: cares about multi-tenant isolation and per-route SLOs; play Dedicated + routing policy combo
Startups frequently focused on dev velocity — lead with SDK parity, quickstart templates, and live-coded migration example
recommended_play: One-route pilot (2–4 weeks): onboard a single non-critical feature, measure latency and cost delta, present results to platform owner
Migration play: 'lift-and-pin' — preserve model id, flip routing with canary percentage, verify metrics, graduate to full cutover
Upsell play for enterprises: start with Hosted for speed, propose Dedicated for predictable bursts, and Private for compliance as a long-term roadmap
